text:
hana: quick share — saw a regression on reranker/embeddings endpoint after the kernel-selection change earlier today. p95 up ~15%, tail ops spiking around kernel-switch boundaries. dashboard: https://perf.redwood/example/rs-1745 :thinking_face:

alex: ugh. can you paste p50/p95/p99 numbers? and is this on dedicated or staging?

hana: staging only so far. p50 ~12ms -> 14ms, p95 ~40ms -> 46ms, p99 120ms -> 155ms. throughput steady.

perf-bot: perf/profile dump available: flame: /artifacts/flame_1790011111.svg, kernel-switch overhead ~6-8ms per switch, small-batch syscall spikes.

maria: hmm KV cache behaviour might be biting us here — rerank/embeds are non-chat single-shot; KV cache priming isn't helpful but our batching heuristic still assumes reuse and pads sequences, causing extra kernel microcalls.

sahil: +1. the continuous-batcher currently groups by arrival-time + fill-to-n-tokens. for non-chat embeds we should prefer a small fixed-token-budget per-window and aggressive token-aware grouping to avoid kernel-switch churn.

alex: can we try: per-endpoint policy override for non-chat rerankers: token_budget_window=256, max_batch_tokens=1024, prefer_homogeneous-token-buckets=true ?

hana: trying a quick config patch in staging now. patch gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/sha123

sahil: also check kernel selection metric: when small batches hit quantized-kernel fallback we pay an extra dispatch. maybe bias selection toward fused-ops kernel for <512 tokens to reduce dispatch count.

maria: note: kv-cache eviction policy currently triggers if batch_count>1 for single-shot requests. that causes allocate/free churn. suggest: for non-chat endpoints set kv_cache.enabled=false or kv_cache.lazy=false.

hana: ran the experiment (staging, two hours): p95 down to 39ms from 46ms, p99 down to 130ms, avg per-request kernel switches reduced by ~40%. CPU sys % reduced.

alex: nice. can you paste the exact continuous-batcher config you used?

hana: config snippet:
```
continuous_batcher: 
  window_ms: 12
  token_budget_strategy: fixed_per_window
  fixed_token_budget: 256  # target tokens per-window for rerank endpoints
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
  max_requests_per_batch: 64
  prefer_homogeneous_tokens: true
  queue_policy: fifo_with_token_backoff
```

sahil: mpi note: fifo_with_token_backoff prevents head-of-line blocking by letting later short requests leapfrog when head is large. reduced HOL waits in the trace.

maria: let's add an endpoint-level knob: kernel_selection_bias: {small_batch: fused_ops, large_batch: default}. avoids the small-kernel dispatch overhead.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert cleared in staging after 30m with new config.

alex: plan: cherry-pick config, run canary on dedicated (10% traffic) for 6h, then rollout if stable. create a release note entry and add an observability metric for kernel-switch-count per-endpoint.

hana: will open PR + canary job. thanks all. :rocket:

sahil: also add a test in loadtest harness that simulates single-shot embed/reranker traffic shape (spikey arrivals, short tokens). catches regressions earlier.

maria: noted — I'll add kv-cache toggle coverage.

hana: tagging @eng-sre for canary runway and @eng-runtime for visibility.

alex: perfect. follow-up sync tomorrow if any canary surprises.
